guard: The migration record: an id derived from the report, a report filed once, an application that is a separate create-only act, and a history ordered by when it happened.
proveWith: pnpm mutation-proof --config packages/core/smoke/mutations/migration-record.json   # --config resolves against the repo root, never the cwd

mutations.name: the id ignores what the check found, so two decisions share one identity
mutations.replace: return digestId(canonicalJson({ v: value.v, run: value.run, toHash: value.toHash }));
mutations.expectRed: and so is a different orphan table, which is the thing a person authorised
mutations.cell: and so is a different orphan table, which is the thing a person authorised

mutations.name: a differing report is written over instead of refused
mutations.expectRed: a DIFFERENT report under the same id is refused rather than overwritten
mutations.cell: a DIFFERENT report under the same id is refused rather than overwritten

mutations.name: the application overwrites whichever driver claimed it first
mutations.find:
const already = existing?.status === undefined ? undefined : parseStatus(existing.status.value, statusKey);
    if (already?.by === by) return;
mutations.expectRed: a DIFFERENT driver claiming it loses loudly: a run moves once
mutations.cell: a DIFFERENT driver claiming it loses loudly: a run moves once

mutations.name: a driver's own retry is treated as a race
mutations.expectRed: the SAME driver re-applying is its own earlier attempt, not a race
mutations.cell: the SAME driver re-applying is its own earlier attempt, not a race

mutations.name: applying a migration nobody filed invents one
mutations.find:
if (merged === undefined)
    throw new EpEnvelopeError("failed-precondition", `no migration is filed at ${specKey}; an application names the migration it applied`);
mutations.replace:
if (merged === undefined && false)
    throw new EpEnvelopeError("failed-precondition", `no migration is filed at ${specKey}; an application names the migration it applied`);
mutations.expectRed: applying a migration nobody filed is a failed precondition, not a new record
mutations.cell: applying a migration nobody filed is a failed precondition, not a new record

mutations.name: the history is ordered by id rather than by when it happened
mutations.find: found.sort((a, b) => (a.spec.at - b.spec.at) || (a.migrationId < b.migrationId ? -1 : a.migrationId > b.migrationId ? 1 : 0));
mutations.expectRed: the earlier DECISION comes first even though its id sorts later
mutations.cell: the earlier DECISION comes first even though its id sorts later

mutations.name: the closed schema lets an unknown field through
mutations.find:
if (!SPEC_KEYS.includes(k))
      throw new EpEnvelopeError("internal", `migration ${key} carries the unknown field "${k}"; record schemas are closed`);
mutations.replace:
if (!SPEC_KEYS.includes(k) && false)
      throw new EpEnvelopeError("internal", `migration ${key} carries the unknown field "${k}"; record schemas are closed`);
mutations.expectRed: an unknown field is refused rather than read past: record schemas are closed
mutations.cell: an unknown field is refused rather than read past: record schemas are closed

unkillable.name: the history is not scoped to the run
unkillable.why: Unkillable by construction, and recorded rather than dropped from the denominator. `recordSpecKey` validates every qualifier as an id token, so a mutation that loosens the run token does not run at all; every other way of widening the prefix collapses into the empty-list failure that a different cell already names. Two enumerations, one structural guard, zero independent kills.
